subject: Urgent: Skyward Health production errors & throughput drop — throttle policy mismatch
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@skywardhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyward Health Support <ops@skywardhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:07 -0700
Subject: High error rate + throttling observed in production (region: us-west)

Hi Mina —

We started seeing a surge in 429/500 errors and a large latency increase across our prod traffic to your API at ~08:45 PT. Throughput has dropped ~40% for a subset of routes (model/text-gen-16k), and clients report long tail latencies. Attached are a small sample of error snippets and a traffic snapshot.

Key points:
- Error spike: 08:45–09:05 PT, ~2.8% 5xx and ~6% 429s during the window.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (text-gen-16k), some streaming connections reset.
- We did not change traffic patterns from our side.

We need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA to restore steady throughput. Please treat this as P1 for Skyward.

Samir
Director, Platform Reliability
Skyward Health

Attachments: skyward_error_snippets.log (text), traffic_snapshot.csv (csv)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@skywardhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:00:21 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throttling observed in production (region: us-west)

Thanks Samir — I pulled the attachments and started a triage. Marcus/Karthik/Laura, looping you in for immediate help.

Initial observations:
- Skyward traffic anomaly lines up with a config change we deployed to the rate limiter (burst window semantics) at 08:30 PT this morning.
- The change tightened burst refill behavior for token-bucket buckets when a quota is exceeded in short windows — this was intended to limit noisy neighbors but may be too aggressive for streaming/long requests.
- Affected customers seem to be hitting the smaller per-route bucket (short burst window) and then getting dropped when the KV cache for the token bucket is cold.

Ask for eng: please review the 08:30 rate-config diff and confirm whether the new burst policy could generate those 429s in a high-multiplexing streaming workload.

I will keep Skyward updated and propose an emergency mitigation after we confirm.

— Mina
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@skywardhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:20:34 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throttling observed in production (region: us-west)

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 10:00 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Initial observations:
> - Change deployed at 08:30 tightened burst refill behavior for token-bucket buckets when a quota is exceeded in short windows.

Confirmed — I pulled the rollout and the diff for the rate-limiter recipe. The change introduced two things that together produced the behavior you see:

1) Burst-window shrink: default burst window for per-route buckets went from 10s -> 2s when traffic is high (this increases chance that long requests outlive the bucket refill cadence).
2) Cold KV gating: to reduce write amplification we added a gating rule that delays token-bucket state rehydration for up to 1s on underpopulated shards. That interacts badly with streaming connections that open many concurrent tokens.

When the two combine, you can see spikes of 429s and elevated latency as clients retry and then encounter queueing on the primary pool.

Immediate mitigation I recommend (safe, reversible):
- Rollback burst-window shrink in the rate-config to previous defaults for the affected customer route groups (canary to Skyward first).
- Temporarily enable an emergency override that routes Skyward to the regional dedicated pool without the gating optimization.
- Short-term: increase per-route burst allowance by +30% and add a soft backoff to reduce concurrent token acquisition pressure.

I can push the rollback now to a small canary; need ops approval to route Skyward to the dedicated pool (this will increase cost but restore service).

— Marcus
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@skywardhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 12:05:12 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throttling observed in production (region: us-west)

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with what I see in the audit logs.

Operational steps I propose now:
- ACTION 1 (urgent, ops): Approve routing Skyward traffic to the regional dedicated pool (manual override). Ops: please confirm capacity.
- ACTION 2 (engineering): Apply config rollback for the burst window on the canary route (target: 10–15 minutes to verify at scale).
- ACTION 3 (CS/AM): Communicate to Skyward that we're prioritizing mitigation and will propose a goodwill credit if their SLA was impacted.

I'll prepare the rollback change and the runbook for the routing override. Marcus — once you confirm the canary command I will execute. Mina — can you confirm you'd like me to proceed with the override if ops confirms capacity?

— Karthik
Director, Platform Engineering
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:30:02 -0700
Subject: RE: High error rate + throttling observed in production (region: us-west)

Samir — quick status update: we traced the cause to a recent rate-limiter change (burst-window + gating optimization) that unintentionally penalized long-lived streaming requests. Marcus and Karthik have validated the fault and proposed immediate mitigations.

What we are doing now:
- Executing a canary rollback of the burst-window change for Skyward routes (10–15m monitoring).
- Preparing a routing override to move Skyward to the regional dedicated pool if the canary doesn't stabilize throughput.
- Monitoring with higher sampling and extended tracing; we will share results within 30 minutes.

We attached our emergency mitigation plan and the hubspot case for reference. We'll follow up with a post-mortem once the incident is contained.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll make this right.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation summary: Skyward Health — production throughput and errors (action requested)

Team — escalate for executive attention and sign-off on customer remediation. Summary:
- Impact: Skyward Health experienced a production throughput drop (~40%) and elevated 429/500 error rates on Oct 12 following a rate-config change to burst-window semantics.
- Root cause: Interaction between a tightened burst-window and a KV gating optimization for token-bucket state leading to token starvation for long-lived streaming requests.
- Mitigation performed: Canary rollback + temporary routing override to regional dedicated pool. Canaries validated restored throughput to baseline; full rollback completed.

Requested approvals:
1) Approve a one-time credit to Skyward: 20% of October usage (goodwill for SLA exposure).
2) Approve a temporary SLA exception for the incident window (Oct 12 08:30–10:00 PT).
3) Approve an immediate post-mortem and timeline for customer communication (draft to be provided by Mina).

I recommend we offer the credit and the SLA exception to retain trust — Skyward is strategic in our healthcare vertical.

— Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
